title: An item
description: What every kind of item shares: name, status, reason and replaced-by, the condition on a retired item, and the patterns of the identifiers; and the statement and the explanation, which a rule and a principle share. The schema of each kind references this file and adds only what is its own; no item file is checked against this file alone.

name.description: A speaking name: lowercase words joined by hyphens. It may change; only the identifier counts.

status.description: planned: published and citable, binds nobody until a pull request makes it active. active: in force. retired: the file stays.

replaced-by.description: The item of the same kind that took the place of a retired item. The schema of the kind fixes its pattern.

rule-id.description: The identifier of a rule: R and four digits from 0001, a fifth digit only after 9999.

definition-id.description: The identifier of a definition: D and four digits from 0001, a fifth digit only after 9999.

principle-id.description: The identifier of a principle: P and four digits from 0001, a fifth digit only after 9999.

group-id.description: The identifier of a group: G and four digits from 0001, a fifth digit only after 9999.

statement.description: One plain sentence on one line, ending with a full stop. Reasons and examples never stand in it. It carries no Markdown but code spans and references in the short form, [some words][D0003] or [R0042]: a square bracket outside a code span stands only in such a reference.

explanation.description: How to read and apply the statement, as Markdown text without headings. It cannot widen what binds; its change is editorial.
